what: Thin uppercase one-line band — after .3s the letters each slide in from outside the right edge of their cell (101%) at 15ms intervals over .4s ease-out, while the band rushes for 3 seconds (the first 30% speeds up quartically to 3.75rem/frame, the last 70% settles down cubically). After that it runs at .1rem/frame and adds the scrolled speed × .2 to that frame, up to .3rem on PC · .0625rem on phone (cooling by .8× each frame)
ease: Rush: first 30% speeds up as r⁴ · last 70% settles as (1−r)³ / text: ease-out

options.rush: Rush duration (seconds), default 3 — 0 skips the rush and goes straight to normal speed
options.wait: Seconds after sticking until the text and rush begin, default .3
options.reveal: Time for one letter to come in (s), default .4
options.boost: Multiplier applied to scroll speed, default .2
options.max: Speed cap added on PC (rem/frame), default .3
options.max-narrow: Speed cap added at 767px and below (rem/Frame), default .0625
options.decay: Extra speed share left per frame, default .8

use: Your statement here. Short and calm.

from.where: index.js [data-marquee] strip below the hero, ‹light surface · heavy meaning›. Original Marquee settings (baseSpeed .1 · rushDurationS 3 · rushDelayMs 300 · charRevealStaggerMs 15 · charRevealDurationMs 400 · scrollVelocityRate .2 · pcMaxBoost .3 · spMaxBoost .0625 · scrollDecay .8). The site starts after the opening ends and adds in the Lenis velocity.

note: The part measures extra speed from the window scroll difference (px/frame). The original measures it with Lenis velocity — sites using Lenis also get scroll events, so the result is nearly the same
